interview.question: Which first country would you pick for Axle, and why?
answer: Germany: VW and Elli V2G launch shows demand, and I would test §14a access.
I would score markets on rules, device base and revenue, as I did at NESO.
GB lessons from Ofgem and Cornwall Insight show how flexibility rules can shift fast.

learn.title: Germany's balancing markets: FCR, aFRR, mFRR
bullets: FCR (frequency containment reserve) reacts in seconds and is paid for capacity.
aFRR (automatic frequency restoration reserve) follows a grid signal, within minutes.
mFRR (manual frequency restoration reserve) is called by the operator, slower, and easier for small fleets.
learn.so_what: Knowing which product a home battery fleet can serve helps you model German revenue per device.

moves.text: Read the Elli V2G launch story and note how the €720 payment works; expect an interview question.
Follow Elli on LinkedIn and watch who partners with it on V2G in Germany.
Skim the Cornwall Insight flexibility piece and draft a LinkedIn comment with your NESO view.

takeaways.text: VW pays German drivers for V2G, so car makers now compete with Axle for home flexibility.
Italy's MACSE storage prices fell 12%, so grid batteries may squeeze flexibility revenues.
UK small batteries near double the record, so GB home flexibility supply is growing fast.

top3.headline: VW pays drivers for home V2G
bullets: Elli V2G programme starts in Germany in December 2026.
Drivers can earn up to €720 in the first year.
top3.why: A car maker is bundling flexibility payments, so it is both a rival and a possible partner.
top3.use: Cite this in interviews as proof home flexibility is going mainstream in Germany.

top3.headline: VW and Elli launch €1,995 V2G wallbox
bullets: Launch covers VW, VW Commercial Vehicles, Cupra and Skoda.
top3.why: Cheap bidirectional hardware makes car batteries a bigger flexibility pool across several brands.
top3.use: Add Elli to your competitor and partner map before any Axle interview.

top3.headline: GB flexibility markets keep evolving
bullets: Cornwall Insight reviews current changes in GB flexibility markets.
Your former employer is tracking this space.
top3.why: GB is Axle's home market, so rule changes affect its revenue and your credibility.
top3.use: Read it and note two points to raise with Axle.

top3.headline: UK home batteries near double record
bullets: MCS data shows 2026 installs close to doubling the annual record.
Policy support is expected to fuel growth in 2027.
top3.why: More home batteries in GB means a bigger base of devices for Axle to control.
top3.use: Quote the MCS figure when discussing GB device growth.

top3.headline: Italy's second storage auction clears lower
bullets: Terna bought 16GWh of long-term BESS capacity.
Price cleared 12% below the first auction.
top3.why: Italy is a likely expansion market, and falling storage prices pressure flexibility revenue.
top3.use: Read up on Italy's MACSE scheme to compare it with other markets.
